The iPhone 18 Pro is just a few months away from its launch. While most iPhone 17 Pro users won't be upgrading so soon, for those considering buying a new iPhone, there are three major features that might attract them to make the switch.

#1: Significant Battery Life Improvements

Longer battery life is often the improvement iPhone users most want to see. Who wouldn't want an iPhone that can go longer between charges?

Last year's iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max already brought notable improvements in this area, but rumours suggest Apple will push battery life even further this year.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are expected to benefit from several performance enhancements: an LTPO+ display, the A20 Pro chip built on a 2nm process, and what may be Apple's in-house C2 cellular modem.

Beyond these improvements, the latest leaks also indicate that this year's Pro models will feature larger physical battery capacities, with the increase on the iPhone 18 Pro Max potentially being particularly significant.

#2: Major Camera Upgrade

Mark Gurman says the iPhone 18 Pro will bring "the biggest camera hardware upgrade in years."

Rumours suggest Apple will focus on upgrading the main and telephoto lenses — the former gaining a new variable aperture feature, and the latter equipped with a wider aperture.

Weibo leaker "Fixed Focus Digital" also recently pointed out that the iPhone 18 Pro's camera platform will be 2mm thicker than the previous generation, due to the "enlarged main lens module," further hinting at major camera changes.

Of course, more specific details would be better at this point, but all signs indicate Apple is preparing some particularly noteworthy camera upgrades.

#3: Design Refinements

Design matters a lot to most people considering upgrading their iPhone every year. If a new iPhone looks almost identical to the model you're currently using, the appeal of upgrading naturally drops significantly.

Although Apple isn't expected to dramatically change the look of the iPhone 17 Pro, the iPhone 18 Pro is reportedly set to receive three design updates:

  • New colour options
  • A slimmer Dynamic Island
  • A unified glass back and aluminium frame

Current rumours point to deep cherry, light blue, and silver, with black/space grey potentially being added.

The iPhone 18 Pro's Dynamic Island is expected to shrink by approximately 35% compared to the previous generation, with a more modern appearance and more usable screen space.

Finally, the much-debated dual-tone back design from last year is expected to be replaced with a more unified look on the iPhone 18 Pro.

Would you consider upgrading from the iPhone 17 Pro to the iPhone 18 Pro? Which factor matters most to you? Let us know in the comments.
